enabled.description: Enable the content filtering plugin. When false, filtering rules are not enforced.

backend.description: Content filtering backend: 'squid' for basic URL filtering via ACLs, 'squidguard' for advanced category-based filtering.

port.description: Port on which the Squid proxy listens for HTTP proxy requests.

conf_path.description: Path to Squid main configuration file. Typically managed by this plugin.

db_path.description: Directory containing SquidGuard category databases (e.g., domains, urls).

url_timeout.description: Seconds to wait for a URL classification lookup before failing open.

db_refresh.description: Seconds between automatic database reload checks.

categories.description: Filtering categories to block by default (e.g., adult, malware, violence). Categories must exist in SquidGuard DB.

ssl_inspection.description: Enable HTTPS traffic inspection via SSL MITM. Increases security coverage but may break some sites and raises privacy considerations.

domains.description: Additional domains to explicitly block, beyond those in category DBs.

exception_groups.description: Unix groups (e.g., 'teachers', 'admin') whose members are exempt from filtering (if supported by auth helper).

level.description: Log verbosity (0=none to 6=debug). Level 2 (error) is recommended for production.

file_path.description: Path to the filter plugin's own log file (not Squid's access.log).

max_kbps.description: Per-client bandwidth limit in KB/s. 0 means unlimited.

max_connections.description: Maximum concurrent connections allowed per client IP.

enabled.description: Use an upstream proxy for outbound connections (e.g., in multi-school deployments).

host.description: Hostname or IP of upstream proxy.
